narrative:
The 2017 Miami Marlins were a team defined by moments of individual brilliance undermined by collective inconsistency, a roster talented enough to flirt with relevance but never quite built to sustain it. Opening April with a 11-12 record, Miami stumbled out of the gate as the pitching staff proved immediately vulnerable, yielding a brutal home run on Opening Day that set an early, ominous tone. But the Fish showed resilience in those first weeks, with J.T. Realmuto, Christian Yelich, and rookie JT Riddle delivering clutch extra-base hits that hinted at a lineup capable of competing.

May brought the Marlins crashing back to earth with a 10-18 collapse, the worst month of their season. The bullpen was the chief culprit — Junichi Tazawa surrendered a grand slam to Yuli Gurriel in Houston that encapsulated everything wrong with the relief corps. Yet even in that wreckage, Tyler Moore's surprise three-run homer offered the kind of unexpected heroics that kept fans believing. June and July were a coin-flip stretch — 14-13 and 14-12 respectively — a .500 grind powered by Marcell Ozuna's emerging star turn and Dee Gordon's speed, but repeatedly sabotaged by the bullpen, including AJ Ramos giving up a devastating three-run Yasiel Puig shot in mid-July.

August was the season's high-water mark, a 17-12 surge that briefly made Wild Card dreams feel tangible. Ozuna hit his 30th home run in a three-run blast that embodied the team's offensive ceiling — Stanton, Ozuna, and Gordon were a legitimate force when the pitching held. But September unraveled everything. An 11-17 fade was driven by bullpen implosions and late-inning disasters, with opposing Phillies and Braves hitters feasting on Miami relievers in pivotal moments. The season ended on a bittersweet note, with Ichiro singling in a Mets game and Justin Bour delivering a clutch hit on the final weekend, but the Marlins finished 77-85, eight games under .500 and watching October from home — a franchise snapshot of what-might-have-been.

chapters.title: Rocky Beginnings
chapters.description: The Marlins open the year with a .500 fight, mixing early bullpen disasters with timely clutch hits from Realmuto, Yelich, and Riddle.

chapters.title: May Meltdown
chapters.description: A brutal 10-18 May exposes the bullpen's fragility, though flashes of offense keep the Marlins from completely falling apart.

chapters.title: Treading Water
chapters.description: June and July produce back-to-back winning records but the team can't break through, as bullpen collapses cancel out Ozuna and Gordon's best moments.

chapters.title: August Surge
chapters.description: The Marlins post their best month at 17-12, with Marcell Ozuna's 30th home run leading a legitimate playoff push.

chapters.title: September Collapse
chapters.description: The bullpen unravels down the stretch as Miami goes 11-17, watching Wild Card hopes evaporate in a string of late-inning disasters.

chapters.title: Fading Into Fall
chapters.description: Ichiro's clutch single and Bour's late heroics offer faint grace notes, but the Marlins close 77-85 and miss the playoffs.
